final_prompt:
I want a habit tracker for myself, to run locally in my browser. It's just me using it: no accounts, no server, data stays on this machine.

Build it as an MVP: the thinnest working slice. Throwaway structure is fine, so don't add abstractions, and don't write tests.

Stack: React with Vite in TypeScript. Persist data in localStorage. It only needs to run locally with the Vite dev server.

Build only these features:
- [ ] Add a habit and delete a habit.
- [ ] Daily check-off: mark a habit done for today (and undo it).
- [ ] Streak count for each habit.
- [ ] A simple 30-day history for each habit.

Do not build reminders or notifications, or charts and stats. The app should use dark mode by default. Leave other styling, naming and edge-case rules to you, and note the choices you make.

Where to build: create a new folder inside the current working directory and put the whole project there. Don't touch anything outside it.

Verify by running it, not just writing it. Start the dev server and click through this flow: add a habit, check it off, see the streak and the 30-day history, then reload the page and confirm the data persists. If you can't drive a browser from here, say so plainly and report what you did check instead. Give the commands you ran and what they showed.

Ask me only if something blocks the listed features. Otherwise decide, keep going, and list your decisions at the end. Local, reversible work needs no confirmation.

You're done when the dev server runs, the click-through above works including persistence after a reload, and you've told me the folder name, the command to start it, and any decisions you made.
